newsitem.title: USA: Clinton spoke to Lott, Gingrich.
newsitem.headline: Clinton spoke to Lott, Gingrich.

text.p: President Clinton spoke to Republican leaders of Congress Friday as he and his top aides attempted to negotiate a balanced budget agreement, the White House said.

Spokesman Mike McCurry said Clinton spoke to House Speaker Newt Gingrich and Senate Majority Leader Trent Lott before leaving the White House to attend a ceremony opening a memorial for Franklin Roosevelt.
He said White House Chief of Staff Erskine Bowles and Treasury Secretary Robert Rubin would be going to Capitol Hill to continue budget negotiations.
Asked if he was ruling out an announcement of a breakthrough Friday, McCurry said: "I'm not ruling it in or out. It's possible, but it's equally possible that there might not be."
He said remaining differences were not just over the size and scope of tax cuts. He said they included other issues which he declined to discuss.

He said Clinton spoke to Lott and Gingrich to express private concerns about an agreement which he later outlined in a statement to reporters in which he said any deal must contain only "disciplined" tax cuts that would not inflate deficits again in the future.
McCurry said Clinton was concerned "about the out-year effects of some of the items under discussion, particularly the impact on deficits beyond the year 2002."
"We must not do anything that would explode the deficit in the out-years beyond 2002, like tax cuts that are structured in a way that do not keep us in a balanced budget environment," McCurry said.
